studies.title: mTOR controls mitochondrial oxidative function through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional complex
studies.authors: Cunningham JT; Rodgers JT; Arlow DH; Vazquez F; Mootha VK; Puigserver P

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed mTOR isn't just about building proteins - it also runs the cell's POWER plants. mTORC1 drives mitochondrial gene expression and oxygen consumption through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional program; block mTOR with rapamycin and mitochondrial output falls. Explains part of why mTOR inhibition reshapes metabolism.

studies.title: Sexual Dimorphism in Placental mTORC1 Signaling, Amino Acid Transport, and Mitochondrial Respiration at Term.
studies.authors: Shimada H; Sakuragi T; Zaegel V; Kramer A; Boyle KE; Powell TL; Jansson T; Rosario FJ

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In 46 term placentas, male placentas showed higher mTORC1 signalling (increased S6RP phosphorylation, reduced 4E-BP1), greater System A amino acid transport and higher mitochondrial respiratory capacity than female placentas, and male pregnancies had a higher birth-weight-to-placental-weight ratio. Observational: a cross-sectional association at a single timepoint, with no intervention and no randomisation, so the direction of the relationship between mTORC1 signalling and growth is not established here and residual confounding by maternal and obstetric factors cannot be excluded.

studies.title: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway regulates mitochondrial oxygen consumption and oxidative capacity
studies.authors: Schieke SM; Phillips D; McCoy JP; Aponte AM; Shen RF; Balaban RS; Finkel T

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human Jurkat T cells (per MeSH); rapamycin; RNAi against TSC2, S6K1, raptor and rictor; subcellular fractionation; 2D-DIGE phosphoproteomics
studies.finding: In human cultured cells, the amount of mTOR-raptor complex correlated with overall mitochondrial activity. Disrupting the complex with rapamycin lowered mitochondrial membrane potential, oxygen consumption and ATP-synthetic capacity. mTOR and mTOR-raptor complexes were found in purified mitochondrial fractions, and rapamycin markedly changed the mitochondrial phosphoproteome. RNA interference against TSC2, S6K1, raptor or rictor led the authors to conclude that mTOR regulates mitochondrial activity independently of its previously known targets, and they proposed that mTOR activity shifts the balance between mitochondrial and non-mitochondrial ATP production. Boundary: Cultured human cell line with acute pharmacological and RNAi manipulation; the link to lifespan is a hypothesis drawn from lower organisms, not tested here. Drafted from the abstract only.

studies.title: L-Arginine Modulates T Cell Metabolism and Enhances Survival and Anti-tumor Activity
studies.authors: Geiger R; Rieckmann JC; Wolf T; Basso C; Feng Y; Fuhrer T; Kogadeeva M; Picotti P; Meissner F; Mann M; Zamboni N; Sallusto F; Lanzavecchia A

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human primary naive CD4 and CD8 T cells with high-resolution metabolomics, proteomics and limited-proteolysis mass spectrometry, plus CRISPR knockout T-cell clones; mouse HA-TCR transgenic transfers with oral L-arginine, and B16-OVA melanoma with OT-I transfer
studies.finding: Tracking metabolites and proteins in activated human T cells, the authors found intracellular L-arginine falls sharply after activation even in 1 mM medium, because uptake and conversion to ornithine, proline and spermidine rise. Raising L-arginine shifted metabolism from glycolysis towards oxidative phosphorylation, increased oxygen consumption and spare respiratory capacity, and produced central-memory-like cells (CCR7 and CD62L high, less IFN-gamma) with greater survival capacity; blocking arginase gave the same survival gain at physiological 150 uM L-arginine. Limited-proteolysis mass spectrometry plus knockout clones identified three nuclear proteins, BAZ1B, PSIP1 and TSN, that sense L-arginine and contribute to the survival programme. In mice, oral L-arginine raised serum levels from about 160 uM to 700 uM and roughly doubled intracellular L-arginine in activated T cells, and L-arginine-treated OT-I cells slowed B16-OVA growth and extended survival. The authors report explicitly that the survival effect was independent of mTOR: L-arginine did not change S6K1 or 4E-BP phosphorylation, and rapamycin, while also improving survival, changed metabolism in an entirely different way. Boundary: mostly human T cells in culture plus mouse transfer and transplantable-tumour models; the dietary arm is a mouse supplementation experiment, not a human trial, and mTOR enters only as a negative control.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 raises mitochondrial respiratory capacity through a YY1–PGC-1α transcriptional programme and through 4E-BP-dependent translation of respiratory components.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 boosts how much energy mitochondria can produce, through both gene activation and protein-building. One mouse experiment points the other way – removing mTORC1 from fat tissue RAISED respiration – so this direction is not settled in a living animal.
relations.boundary: Effect size varies strongly by tissue; the transcriptional and translational arms have not been cleanly separated in vivo. OVERLAP (audit 2026-09-04): this edge and MTORC1-MITO assert overlapping biology from overlapping citations (CUN2007, MOR2013) at different tiers and different consensus levels. Read them together; they are not independent support.
